h1: The 5 Best Monitor Privacy Screen Protectors of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Monitor Privacy Protectors: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five monitor privacy screen protectors from infoWall, Magicmoon, Vxaop and more, compared on mounting, size and pack value.
summary: The infoWall 2-pack is the best monitor privacy filter, a 27 inch pair with a tape-free, washable nano-suction mount that fits curved and flat screens. The Peslv is the removable 24 inch pair, the Magicmoon and Vxaop are cheaper 24 inch pairs, and the SightPro is a single 24 inch filter with anti-glare.
intro: A privacy filter is not a screen protector. It does not guard against scratches; it narrows the angle from which the display is readable, so a colleague leaning over your shoulder or a stranger on a train sees a dark panel. The detail that decides whether you like one is how it attaches. A filter that is awkward to fit or leaves sticky residue ends up in a drawer.

Attachment, size and pack count therefore drive this ranking more than film quality. Five desktop filters were compared from their listings: four are 24 inch, one is 27 inch, and laptop filters were left out. We scored on how clearly the listing explains the mount, whether the size matches common monitors, how many filters you get and which price bucket the pack falls in.

products.name: infoWall 2-Pack 27 Inch Computer Privacy Screen Filter, Nano-Suction Bezel
products.verdict: Tape-free, washable mounting that fits curved and flat 27 inch monitors.
products.description:
The infoWall earns first place by explaining its mount. It is a 2-pack of 27 inch, 16:9 filters held on by a nano-suction bezel, with a tape-free, washable design that the listing says works on both curved and flat monitors. Suction clings without adhesive, so there is no tape to peel or residue left on the monitor frame if you remove it.

The mounting is what separates it from the pack: the other filters here do not describe how they attach, while this one does. It lands in the $50 to $100 range.

Buy it for a 27 inch screen, including a curved one, where a flexible hold matters. The caveat is size: it is the only 27 inch protector in the ranking, so it simply will not fit a 24 inch monitor, and the pair is priced above the cheaper 24 inch options.

products.name: Peslv [2-Pack] 24 Inch Privacy Screen for Computer Monitor, 16:9 Aspect Ratio
products.verdict: A removable 24 inch pair with true side-angle privacy.
products.description:
The Peslv is the 24 inch pair for people who plan to take the filter off. It supplies two 24 inch, 16:9 filters with true side-angle privacy, and the listing describes them as removable. Removable matters when you share your screen with a colleague or want to show work, since you can lift it away and put it back.

It ranks second because it gives you the pair and the removable design, but not the described tape-free mount of the infoWall. Against the cheaper 24 inch pairs below, you pay more, in the $50 to $100 range, for the stated removable design.

Buy it for dual 24 inch desks where you switch between private and shared viewing. The caveat is that mounting detail is thin beyond removability, and the higher price bucket means the Magicmoon is the better choice if budget leads.

products.name: Magicmoon 2-Pack 24 Inch Computer Privacy Screen Filter for 16:9 Monitor
products.verdict: A 24 inch pair at the lower price tier.
products.description:
The Magicmoon is the value pair. It bundles two 24 inch, 16:9 filters with true side-angle privacy, priced in the $25 to $50 range, which makes it a cheap way to cover both screens of a dual-monitor desk. The specs match the Peslv on size and privacy angle for a lower bucket.

It lands third because the listing does not state whether the filters are removable, which is the gap. A filter you cannot easily take off is a problem the moment you need to present a screen or clean the panel.

Choose it for a dual-monitor desk on a budget. The caveat is thin listing detail: no mount description and no removability claim, so check the product page before ordering, and skip it if you share your screen often or want to move the filters between monitors.
products.idealFor: Dual 24 inch monitors on a budget.
products.skipIf: You need to share your screen often.

products.name: Vxaop [2-Pack] 24 Inch Computer Privacy Screen Filter (16:9 Aspect Ratio)
products.verdict: A near-identical 24 inch pair from a lesser-known brand.
products.description:
The Vxaop is nearly a twin of the Magicmoon. It is a 2-pack of 24 inch, 16:9 filters with true side-angle privacy, in the $25 to $50 range. The pair covers two matching monitors, and the price bucket is as low as any here.

It ranks one place below the Magicmoon since the listed specs are identical and the brand is less established. With nothing to separate the two on paper, brand familiarity and an easier path to returns break the tie.

Choose it if you are buying purely on price and it is cheaper than the pair above on the day. The caveat is that nothing here distinguishes it: no mount description, no removability claim, no extra feature. If you want something that explains how it attaches, step up to the Peslv or the infoWall.

products.name: SightPro 24 Inch 16:9 Computer Privacy Screen Filter for Monitor
products.verdict: A single 24 inch filter that adds anti-glare.
products.description:
The SightPro is a single 24 inch, 16:9 filter that offers true side-angle privacy plus an anti-glare layer, in the $25 to $50 range. Anti-glare is the extra none of the pairs list: it cuts reflections from a window or overhead light, which matters when the screen sits in a bright room.

It finishes last because you get one filter, not two, so a dual-monitor desk would need a second purchase. The pairs above cost about the same per box and cover both screens.

Buy it for a single-monitor desk in a bright room, where reflection is a bigger complaint than privacy. The caveat is the missing mount detail: the listing does not say how it attaches or whether it is removable, so check the product page and keep your monitor size in mind.

whatMatters.detail: Nano-suction clings without adhesive and can be washed, while adhesive tabs are more permanent and can leave residue. How a filter attaches decides whether you can remove it for a presentation. Check the listing for tape-free or removable wording, and be cautious where the mount is not described at all, since a bad hold is the usual reason people stop using a filter.

A curved monitor needs a filter that flexes with it, and a rigid one will gap at the edges. Only the infoWall lists support for both curved and flat screens. If you own a curved monitor, verify compatibility before ordering, and ask the seller if the listing is silent on curvature, because curved panels need a flexible filter.

Filters are cut to a diagonal size and a 16:9 ratio, and a wrong size leaves visible gaps or covers part of the bezel. Match the numbers in the title to your monitor, such as 24 inch or 27 inch, and confirm the aspect ratio. A filter that is slightly too small shows uncovered edges that make the privacy effect easy to bypass.

Pairs cost less per screen than singles and suit dual-monitor desks. Count your monitors before choosing between a pair and a single, and remember a spare helps if you move equipment or a filter gets scratched. A single filter only makes sense if you are certain you will use one screen.

Anti-glare cuts reflections from windows and lights, which helps in bright rooms where the screen competes with sunlight. Only the SightPro lists it here. Check for the word if your desk faces a window, because side-angle privacy alone does nothing about reflected light on the panel, and glare can make a dark filter harder to read.

faq.q: Will it leave residue on my monitor?
faq.a: The infoWall is described as tape-free and washable, so it avoids adhesive residue. The other listings do not describe residue, so check the product page before assuming a clean removal, and test a corner first.

Buying on price without checking size. A 24 inch filter such as the Magicmoon or Vxaop will not fit a 27 inch screen, and the infoWall will not fit a 24 inch one. Check the diagonal and the 16:9 ratio before you pay.

faq.q: Is the infoWall worth the extra over the 24 inch pairs?
faq.a: If you have a 27 inch or curved monitor, yes, because it is the only one that fits and lists curved support, and the pair covers two screens. If you have a 24 inch screen, it will not fit at all.

faq.q: How do I put one on?
faq.a: Follow the listing instructions. The infoWall uses a nano-suction bezel rather than adhesive tape, so you clean the screen and press it into place. Wipe off dust first so the suction holds. For the others, check the maker's steps.

The infoWall listing says it is washable. For the Peslv, Magicmoon, Vxaop and SightPro, the listings do not say, so follow the maker's care notes and avoid harsh cleaners or abrasive cloths that scratch the surface.

faq.q: Do these work on a laptop?
faq.a: No. These are sized for desktop monitors. Laptop screens need a filter listed for your exact laptop size, and a mismatch leaves gaps or hides part of the display, so measure before you order.

finalTake: Buy the infoWall if you own a 27 inch monitor, curved or flat. For 24 inch screens, the Peslv gives a stated removable design, and the Magicmoon is the budget pair. Pick the SightPro only for one bright-room monitor, and skip the Vxaop unless it is the cheapest pair on the day.
